title: ephemeral-venv-presubmit-and-release-preflight-smoke-runner
author: Aisha Turner
description:
Motivation: presubmit setup time and noisy global virtualenvs are slowing local feedback and contributing to flaky CI. This PR refactors the presubmit bootstrap to create short-lived, per-language ephemeral virtual environments (venv/virtualenv for Python, isolated node_modules for JS) that are created on-demand and cached per-commit hash. It also introduces a release-preflight smoke-runner that validates signing artifacts, artifact metadata stamping, and the lightweight release path (used by release automation) before the full release pipeline is triggered.

What this changes: ephemeral per-language venv creation logic in tools/ci/bootstrap.py (faster, parallelizable, robust teardown), a small action wrapper that performs lazy dependency install only for changed language scopes, updates to .github/workflows/presubmit.yml to split fast local lint checks vs remote heavyweight lint runners, and a new tools/ci/release-preflight.py that performs a dry-run against release manifests and an artifact verification step. Also bumps two GitHub Actions that were causing provenance warnings.

Design notes: the venv agent uses a commit-hash keyed cache directory and a TTL of 48 hours; CI workers clear stale caches in nightly maintenance. The lazy installer detects changed files via git paths and installs only the minimal subset of devdeps (uses package-dev-manifests under each workspace). Release preflight focuses on deterministic steps: artifact hash validation, signature chain presence (when signing enabled), and version stamping consistency. This is intentionally conservative: the preflight will fail-fast on mismatches and provide deterministic diagnostics for on-call.

Testing and rollout: landed behind a toggle PRESUBMIT_EPHEMERAL=true so we can roll out to a fraction of CI lanes first. Smoke tests were added to the presubmit pipeline to exercise creation/teardown and cache hit/miss behavior. Release preflight is wired into the staging release lane and does not gate production releases until we've observed ~1 week of stable runs.

Notes: minimal surface changes to developers; CONTRIBUTING.md updated with a short troubleshooting section. Linear tickets ENG-2891 (speed up presubmit) and ENG-2905 (release safety) are linked.

feat(ci): add release-preflight smoke-runner and deterministic artifact checks
chore(actions): bump actions/setup-node to v3.7.0 and actions/cache to v4
test(ci): add presubmit smoke tests for venv lifecycle and cache hits
docs: update CONTRIBUTING.md presubmit troubleshooting and toggle docs
review_thread: Evan Morales: Can we make the cache TTL configurable per-repo? Some teams prefer longer-lived caches.
Aisha Turner: Added PRESUBMIT_CACHE_TTL env override (hours) and documented behavior in CONTRIBUTING.md.
Priya Nair: Release preflight looks good, but we should surface signature mismatch diagnostics as structured JSON for the on-call toolchain.
Aisha Turner: release-preflight now emits a compact JSON diagnostics blob when run with --emit-json; included examples in the unit tests.
Liam Chen: Flaky lint runner in the remote lane still failed once in CI rerun — was this investigated?
Aisha Turner: The failure was a transient network fetch to the remote runner. I added a retry and improved logs; reran CI and it passed. See CI checks below.
ci_checks: integration-lint-remote: failed on first run (fetch timeout) -> rerun -> pass
e2e: skipped (fastpath enabled for this PR)
merge_outcome: merged via squash (squash commit: refactor(ci): ephemeral venv bootstrap + release preflight). Merge performed after 2 approvals and green CI; merge commit includes short changelog in body.
release_notes:
- Introduce ephemeral per-language presubmit venvs (faster local feedback, reduced global env pollution)
- Add release-preflight smoke-runner to validate artifact hashes and signatures
- Split presubmit into lightweight local checks and remote heavyweight lanes; add smoke tests
- Bump actions/setup-node and actions/cache (minor hygiene)
notes_for_ops: Nightly cache maintenance job should be monitored during the first week; a quick dashboard tile was added to infra -> ci to surface cache eviction rate and release-preflight failures. If release-preflight emits signature mismatch diagnostics, on-call should follow the signed-artifacts runbook (SEC-RELEASE-RUNBOOK).
